intro.heading: IKAY, your digital fingerprint
intro.content1: Hi, I'm Nando Muñoz, and IKAY was born as a tool to help you see, identify and manage your digital fingerprint.
intro.content2: Below you will find a dashboard with part of the information you hand over to a website every time you visit it through your browser. If you want to know more, go and read my article on the subject (Spanish only 🙁)

main.noSupport: This page couldn't get this one: your browser, or its protections, kept it to itself. One less clue about you.
main.proof: For the curious: how we know

aboutme.heading: About me
aboutme.content1: I'm Nando Muñoz, and I've spent more than ten years building products for big brands as a frontend tech lead. I came to the craft before AI, and I've built frontend teams on Adobe Experience Manager and Salesforce Commerce Cloud.
aboutme.content2: You can reach me on Github, Twitter or Linkedin

footer.title: The state of your data
footer.content1: All the data shown on this website is stored on your device only, and is never sent to any external server. Why? Because I'm not interested in your data, I'm interested in your awareness.
footer.content2: That said, I don't know whether GitHub (the server hosting this website) or ipapi.co (the external API I use to work out your city, country and telecom operator from your IP) store data similar to the one shown here, or any other kind. But hey, if you don't mind sharing every dinner, moment, memory or feeling on Facebook, you probably won't mind the information (much like this) collected about you by that wonderful website where they told you that you can watch paid movies online, but for free :D Allow me a little irony :)
footer.thanks: I want to thank Robin Linus for the inspiration, and Flaticon for their icons

location.title: Where you are, roughly

modalinfo.title: Geolocation
modalinfo.description: IP geolocation makes it possible to track a visitor's location using an IP geolocation database or an API. Visitors can be located down to a city, region or country.

location.plain: Any website can place you on a map from your IP, roughly down to your city, without asking.

device.title: The device you are using

modalinfo.title: Device
modalinfo.description: Identifies the type of device you are connecting from (Android Mobile, Android Tablet, iPad, iPhone, Windows Laptop, Macbook, iMac or Mac Mini, a TV or some other type).

device.plain: Websites adapt what they show you, and sometimes their prices, to the device you use.
device.sentence: The device you're browsing on is {0}.

screen.title: Your screen size

modalinfo.title: Display Resolution
modalinfo.description: The display resolution is the number of distinct pixels that can be shown on the screen. It is given by the width multiplied by the height, which yields a ratio known as the 'aspect ratio'. This aspect ratio can vary depending on the shape of the monitor and on the graphics card.

screen.plain: Your screen size narrows down which device model you have.

orientation.title: How you hold your device

type.undefined: Since you are using a {0}, I can't tell

modalinfo.title: Orientation
modalinfo.description: Tells the orientation of your device, as long as it is a mobile phone or a tablet.

orientation.plain: It tells whether you are holding a phone or tablet, and how.
orientation.sentence: You're holding your device in {0} position.

darkmode.title: Light or dark look

modalinfo.title: Dark Mode
modalinfo.description: This mode noticeably reduces eye strain. It consists of setting the background to a dark shade (black or grey).

darkmode.plain: A small detail, but one more thing that sets you apart from other visitors.
darkmode.systemNote: This is your system setting. You can still pick another look for this page in the menu.

lang.title: Your language

modalinfo.title: Language
modalinfo.description: The language you have set in your browser, and probably on your device too.

lang.plain: Websites use it to guess your country and which language to show you.

exit.title: You left the page...
exit.firsttime: This is your first time on this page.

modalinfo.title: Web Analytics
modalinfo.description: Web analytics is the collection, measurement, analysis and reporting of web data in order to understand and optimise web usage. Web analytics is not just a process for measuring web traffic, though: it is also used to assess and improve the effectiveness of a website.

exit.plain: A website can quietly keep a record of every time you come back.

os.title: Your device's system

modalinfo.title: The Operating System
modalinfo.description: An operating system (OS) is the main software, or set of programs, of a computer system. It manages the hardware resources and provides services to application software, running in a privileged mode with respect to all the rest.

os.plain: Websites can tailor offers, and even some attacks, to the system you use.

browser.title: The program you browse with

modalinfo.title: Browser
modalinfo.description: A web browser is a piece of software, an application or a program that gives you access to the Web, interpreting the information in different kinds of files and websites so that they can be displayed.

browser.plain: Outdated versions can be targeted by attacks, and the exact version helps recognise you.

connection.title: Your internet speed

modalinfo.title: Download speed
modalinfo.description: Connection speed is the average amount of information transmitted between two devices per unit of time in a transmission system. The units used to measure it usually depend on the field being studied. In telecommunications the unit is bits per second (bit/s), and it is quite common to use different magnitudes such as kbit/s (sometimes abbreviated as 'kbps').

connection.plain: A website can tell whether you are on fast fibre or on slow mobile data.

telco.title: Your internet company

modalinfo.title: Your Internet provider
modalinfo.description: A telephone company, also known as a telco, telephone service provider, or telecommunications operator, is a kind of communications service provider (CSP), more precisely a telecommunications service provider (TSP), that provides telecommunications services such as telephony and data communications access. Many telephone companies were at one time government agencies or privately owned but state-regulated monopolies. The government agencies are often referred to, primarily in Europe, as PTTs (postal, telegraph and telephone services).

telco.plain: It reveals your internet company, and whether you connect from home, from work or on mobile data.

ip.title: Your internet address (IP)

modalinfo.title: IP
modalinfo.description: An Internet Protocol address (IP address) is a numerical label assigned to each device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication. An IP address serves two main functions: host or network interface identification, and location addressing.

ip.plain: It works like a postal address: it roughly locates you and can link your visits together.
ip.sentence: Your address on the internet is {0}.

ram.title: Your device's memory

modalinfo.title: RAM Memory
modalinfo.description: Random-access memory (RAM) is used as the working memory of computers and other devices, for the operating system, the programs and most of the software. Every instruction executed by the central processing unit and by other units of the computer is loaded into RAM, which also holds the data those programs work with.

ram.plain: It hints at how powerful and expensive your device is; some shops have been accused of adjusting prices to that.
ram.sentence: Your device has about {0} of RAM.

cpu.title: Your device's processor

modalinfo.title: Processor
modalinfo.description: The microprocessor (or simply the processor) is the most complex central integrated circuit of a computer system. By way of illustration, it is often called, by analogy, the 'brain' of a computer.

cpu.plain: More cores usually means a newer, pricier device, and one more detail that tells you apart.

gpu.title: Your graphics card

modalinfo.title: The Graphics Card
modalinfo.description: A graphics card is an expansion card on the computer's motherboard which processes the data coming from the central processing unit (CPU) and turns it into information that can be understood and displayed on the output device (for example: a monitor, a television or a projector). These cards use a graphics processing unit, or GPU, a term often used incorrectly to refer to the graphics card itself.
modalinfo.moreinfo: More info about the graphics card

gpu.plain: The exact name of your graphics card is rare enough to help recognise your device.
gpu.sentence: Your graphics card introduces itself as {0}.

battery.title: Your battery

modalinfo.title: Battery API
modalinfo.description: The Battery Status API, more often referred to as the Battery API, provides information about the system's battery charge level and lets you be notified by events that are sent when the battery level or charging status change. This can be used to adjust your app's resource usage to reduce battery drain when the battery is low, or to save changes before the battery runs out in order to prevent data loss.

battery.plain: Your battery level can help recognise you across websites for a few minutes.

fingerprint.title: Your invisible ID code

type.note: This code comes from mixing the stable data on this page. I don't store it anywhere: it is computed again on every visit and it comes out the same. That is the problem.

modalinfo.title: Your cookieless fingerprint
modalinfo.description: Browser fingerprinting: by putting together data your browser hands over without asking (screen, fonts, GPU, time zone, how it paints a canvas...) you get an almost unique identifier. It uses no cookies, so deleting them or opening incognito mode does not change it. That is how you can be followed across websites without noticing.

fingerprint.plain: Mix everything below and you get a code that recognises you on every visit, even without cookies.

timezone.title: Your time zone

type.match: Matches the time zone of your IP ({0})
type.mismatch: Does not match the one of your IP ({0}): are you using a VPN or a proxy?

modalinfo.title: Time zone
modalinfo.description: The time zone comes from your operating system. If it does not match the one of your IP, that is a clear hint that you are using a VPN or a proxy, something many websites look for.

timezone.plain: Your clock reveals roughly where you live, even if you hide your IP.
timezone.sentence: Your browser places you in the {0} time zone.

locale.title: How you write dates and numbers

modalinfo.title: Regional format
modalinfo.description: How you write numbers, dates and times (1,234.5 or 1.234,5; 24h or AM/PM; calendar) depends on the regional settings of your system. Together with your preferred languages, it says a lot about where you are from.

locale.plain: It hints at the country you come from, even when you travel.
locale.sentence: You write dates and numbers the {0} way.

display.title: Your browser window

modalinfo.title: Window and screen
modalinfo.description: Besides the resolution, the website sees the pixel density, the size of your window, the space taken by the taskbar or the dock, the color gamut, whether your screen is HDR and, in some browsers, whether you have more than one monitor.

display.plain: Window size, pixel density, colours: small details that together tell devices apart.

preferences.title: Your accessibility settings

modalinfo.title: Accessibility
modalinfo.description: Your accessibility preferences (less motion, more contrast, forced colors...) are available to any website through CSS. They help adapt the design, but each one that is not the default makes you easier to tell apart.

preferences.plain: If you changed any of them, you become easier to tell apart from everyone else.
preferences.sentence: You have {0} in your accessibility settings.

input.title: Mouse or touch screen

type.both: a mouse and a touch screen

modalinfo.title: How you interact
modalinfo.description: The website knows whether you use a mouse or trackpad, a touch screen or both, whether you can hover over things and how many fingers your screen detects at once.
modalinfo.moreinfo: More info about the pointer media query

input.plain: It gives away whether you are on a phone, a tablet or a computer.
input.sentence: You get around the web with {0}.

keyboard.title: Your keyboard

modalinfo.title: Keyboard layout
modalinfo.description: In Chromium-based browsers, the Keyboard API tells which character each physical key produces. That reveals whether your keyboard is QWERTY, AZERTY, QWERTZ... one more hint about your country.

keyboard.plain: Your keyboard layout is one more hint about your country.

canvas.title: A hidden drawing test

type.caption: Your browser has just drawn this image without you seeing it. The code above sums up exactly how it came out.

modalinfo.title: Canvas fingerprint
modalinfo.description: The website secretly draws the same image in every browser. Your GPU, its drivers, your system and your fonts paint it with differences you cannot see, but the hash of the image changes from one device to another.

canvas.plain: Your computer draws images in its own tiny, unique way. That is enough to recognise you.
canvas.sentence: Your browser's hidden drawing boils down to {0}.

audio.title: A silent sound test

modalinfo.title: Audio fingerprint
modalinfo.description: Without playing anything, the website generates a sound in memory (OfflineAudioContext) and adds up its samples. Every combination of browser, system and hardware rounds differently, so the final number helps tell you apart.

audio.plain: Your device processes sound in its own tiny way, which also helps recognise it.
audio.sentence: Your device turned the silent sound into {0}.

fonts.title: Typefaces on your computer

modalinfo.title: Typefaces on your computer
modalinfo.description: By measuring the width of a text with each typeface (techies call them fonts), the website finds out which ones you have installed without asking. It reveals your operating system and programs like Office or Adobe.

fonts.plain: The typefaces you installed hint at your job and your apps (Office, Adobe…).
fonts.sentence: We found {0} installed on your computer.
fonts.protected: Your browser {0} which typefaces you have installed.
fonts.listLabel: Here they are, each in its own lettering (techies call them fonts):

voices.title: Reading-aloud voices

modalinfo.title: Speech voices
modalinfo.description: The list of voices to read text aloud comes from your operating system and from the language packs you installed. It is very different from one device to another.

voices.plain: The voices on your system reveal it, and the languages you have installed.

incognito.title: Private browsing

modalinfo.title: Incognito mode
modalinfo.description: The storage space the browser gives each website is different in incognito mode. By comparing it, a website can guess whether you browse privately. In Chromium it also hints at the size of your disk.

incognito.plain: Websites can often tell when you browse privately.

adblock.title: Ad blocker

type.win: Nice! You have an ad blocker: fewer ads and fewer trackers following you.
type.nudge: No ad blocker here. Installing one cuts down the trackers that follow you around.

modalinfo.title: Ad blocker
modalinfo.description: The website creates an empty element with classes that look like an ad. If a blocker hides it, the page notices. Useful for you, but also one more piece of data about you.

adblock.plain: Websites can nag you, hide content or simply note it down as one more trait.

signals.title: “Don't track me” requests

modalinfo.title: Privacy signals
modalinfo.description: Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control ask websites not to track you, but honouring them is voluntary. The irony: turning them on makes you a little easier to tell apart. It also shows whether you accept cookies, have a PDF viewer and whether the browser is automated.
modalinfo.moreinfo: More info about Global Privacy Control

signals.plain: Respecting “do not track” is optional for websites, and turning it on makes you a bit more unique.
signals.sentence: Your browser sends these “don't track me” requests: {0}.

navigation.title: How you got here

modalinfo.title: Your browsing
modalinfo.description: The website knows how many pages you visited in this tab, which website you came from and whether you reloaded or went back.

navigation.plain: A website can see which page sent you here and how you move around.

behaviour.title: What you do on this page

type.caption: I don't save any of this: I only show you what any website could record. The box is your screen in miniature.

modalinfo.title: What you do here
modalinfo.description: Any website can record your mouse movements, clicks, scroll, keys and when you switch tabs, without asking. Some record the whole session to watch it later (session replay).

behaviour.plain: Any website can record your mouse, clicks and scroll, and even replay your visit later.
behaviour.sentence: So far you have moved your mouse {0} times here.

summary.title: Your file, so far
summary.points: data points your browser gave away
summary.blocked: Well done: {0} points in favour of your privacy.
summary.note: Everything is worked out inside your browser. Only your IP goes to ipapi.co (for the location), and the map is loaded from Google.
summary.private: points in favour of your privacy
